SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Patient is a 66-year-old female presenting with low back pain. She reports onset of low back pain on 03/16/2025. Denies any trauma or neurologic symptoms. Started NSAIDs on 03/17/2025. Plans to begin physical therapy on 03/23/2025. Exam shows normal lower-extremity strength, reflexes, and sensation. Assessment: acute low back pain without radiculopathy. Plan: Continue NSAIDs, start PT as scheduled, follow up in 2 weeks.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Return visit for low back pain. NSAIDs were started on 03/17/2025 and discontinued on 05/11/2025 with partial response. Physical therapy was initiated on 03/23/2025, completed 14 sessions, and ended on 05/11/2025 with no improvement. Denies new neurologic symptoms. Exam unchanged. Assessment: persistent low back pain despite conservative measures. Plan: Consider MRI lumbar spine to further evaluate; continue symptomatic care.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Follow-up visit after completion of conservative therapy. The patient denies trauma, cancer, fever, weight loss, bladder or bowel symptoms, saddle anesthesia, and progressive neurologic deficit. NSAIDs were started on 03/17/2025 and discontinued on 05/11/2025 with partial response. Physical therapy was initiated on 03/23/2025, completed 14 sessions, and ended on 05/11/2025 with no improvement. Spine surgery referral is under consideration pending MRI findings. Exam: stable, no change in strength or reflexes. Assessment: inadequate response to NSAIDs and physical therapy. Plan: Order lumbar MRI today to assess for structural pathology; await results before definitive intervention.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
Order for lumbar MRI placed today 06/02/2025. Patient continues to experience low back pain despite NSAIDs and physical therapy. No new neurologic deficits. Spine surgery referral is under consideration pending MRI findings. Assessment: need imaging to guide possible surgical referral. Plan: Perform lumbar MRI; review results and discuss with patient.
